short: Takeda sites repeat work done elsewhere
name: Takeda sites repeat work done elsewhere
why: Teams face similar problems with equipment breakdowns, slow batch release and cleanroom training. They may start from scratch without knowing what another Takeda site has already learned.
pattern: Takeda has published three network programmes for exactly these problems: AI predictive maintenance at Lessines (170+ agents across 45 systems, extension to 20 sites planned by FY2027), VR/AR operator training at 13 sterile-filling sites, and One Day Batch Release piloted at six sites.
state: Published Takeda programmes exist for this problem. They are not proof that the 60 illustrative voices are solved, or that a given plant is in scope or qualified.
route: Name the programme owner (Digital Manufacturing, GSQ operator training or One Day Batch Release), ask whether your plant is in scope, and confirm the qualification it still needs.

name: Teams build their own AI tools instead of using what Takeda already offers
why: Colleagues in Legal, Finance, Commercial, R&D and plants describe building or buying separate AI helpers, unsure which tool is allowed, what data it may see and who must review it.
pattern: Takeda reports 63% of employees actively using generative-AI tools (2026), an internal assistant, myAibou, designed to see only what the user types, and a Responsible AI framework with assessments run together with Ethics & Compliance.
state: An enterprise assistant and a Responsible AI assessment route are published. Whether a specific team's need is covered still requires DD&T and Ethics & Compliance review.
route: Before building, check the approved enterprise assistant, then run a Responsible AI and privacy impact assessment with DD&T and Ethics & Compliance.
proofLabel: Published route, confirm your use case

name: Each launch country re-learns how to educate doctors about a new medicine
why: Medical and field teams in each next market ask how to explain a first-in-class medicine, which materials are approved and what the first countries learned — and often start again.
pattern: ORZEYFUL became available in Japan and China on the same day, 15 October 2026, and Japan publishes a data-driven model for HCP information. The clinical evidence is shared; approved claims and populations differ by country.
state: Related public work exists. No approved cross-country education asset is published, and claims cannot travel between labels.
route: Ask the first-launch Medical teams which physician questions came up, then let Medical and Legal in the receiving country review label, audience and claims.
proofLabel: Related work only — no proven fit

name: Patients wait too long for a diagnosis, and each country maps the referral path alone
why: Access and Medical teams describe the same barrier — patients move between doctors for years before reaching the right specialist — yet each country builds its own patient-pathway map.
pattern: Takeda's 2026 report lists disease awareness, screening and diagnosis among the access barriers it works on, and a 2026 Takeda account describes physician experience with narcolepsy type 1. No shared cross-country referral map is published.
state: Takeda publishes the ambition and disease context, not a product-specific referral pathway for any country.
route: Medical, Market Access and patient-group leads compare pathway maps from first-launch countries before commissioning a new one.
proofLabel: Related work only — no proven fit

name: Know-how and the reasons behind decisions leave when people change roles
why: Across functions, colleagues inherit work without the 'why': past decisions, who to ask and what was already tried disappear when someone moves on.
pattern: Takeda documents mentoring, Career Navigator, over 2,000 values ambassadors and HR digital agents used by about 60% of employees with a Takeda device. None of these records the reasoning behind a past decision.
state: Learning and mentoring are documented; a shared record of decision reasoning is not. This is the gap MIERU's decision memory proposes to fill.
route: HR and functional leads pilot a one-page decision-handover record at real role changes and measure whether the next owner reopens the same question.
proofLabel: Related work only — no proven fit
